#!/usr/bin/env bash
# ============================================================
# GRIMDARK PAKKE v1 — warpstorm.online one-shot deploy
# Kører: settings → plugins → tema → kategorier → sider → CSS
#        → permalinks/frontpage (helper) → artikel 1-5 som drafts
# Brug:  bash deploy.sh [BASE_URL]
# Kræver: AUTH i env eller /workspace/warpstorm/.wp-auth-online ("user:app-password")
# Env:   PUBLISH=1 (udgiv i stedet for drafts) · JETPACK=1 · SHORTPIXEL=1
# Idempotent: kan genkøres — eksisterende objekter springes over.
# ============================================================
set -u
BASE="${1:-https://warpstorm.online}"
HERE="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")" && pwd)"
AUTH_FILE="${AUTH_FILE:-/workspace/warpstorm/.wp-auth-online}"
AUTH="${AUTH:-}"
[ -z "$AUTH" ] && [ -f "$AUTH_FILE" ] && AUTH="$(head -1 "$AUTH_FILE" | tr -d ' \r\n')"
if [ -z "$AUTH" ]; then echo "FEJL: ingen auth. Opret $AUTH_FILE med 'bruger:app-password'"; exit 1; fi

STATUS_DRAFT="draft"; [ "${PUBLISH:-0}" = "1" ] && STATUS_DRAFT="publish"
SLEEP="${SLEEP:-3}"
MAP="$HERE/lib/catmap.env"; mkdir -p "$HERE/lib"; : > "$MAP"
FAILS=0

api() { # api METHOD PATH [JSON_BODY]
  local m="$1" p="$2" b="${3:-}" code out
  out="$(curl -sS -u "$AUTH" -X "$m" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        ${b:+--data "$b"} -o "$HERE/lib/last.json" -w "\n%{http_code}" \
        "$BASE/wp-json$p" 2>&1)" || { echo "  ! curl-fejl: $out"; return 1; }
  code="$(printf '%s' "$out" | tail -1)"
  if [ "$code" = "429" ] || [ "$code" = "503" ]; then
    echo "  … rate-limit ($code) — venter 60s og prøver igen"; sleep 60
    out="$(curl -sS -u "$AUTH" -X "$m" -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
          ${b:+--data "$b"} -o "$HERE/lib/last.json" -w "\n%{http_code}" "$BASE/wp-json$p")" && code="$(printf '%s' "$out" | tail -1)"
  fi
  [ "$code" = "200" ] || [ "$code" = "201" ] || { echo "  ! HTTP $code på $m $p"; head -c 300 "$HERE/lib/last.json"; echo; return 1; }
  return 0
}

get_id_by_slug() { # get_id_by_slug TYPE SLUG → id eller tom
  local type="$1" slug="$2" id
  api GET "/wp/v2/$type?slug=$slug&status=draft,publish,future,private&per_page=1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || { api GET "/wp/v2/$type?slug=$slug&per_page=1" >/dev/null 2>&1 || return 0; }
  id="$(jq -r '.[0].id // empty' "$HERE/lib/last.json" 2>/dev/null)"
  printf '%s' "$id"
}

echo "== 0/8 Preflight =="
api GET "/wp/v2/users/me?context=edit" >/dev/null || { echo "FEJL: auth afvist af $BASE"; exit 1; }
jq -r '"  auth: " + .name + " (id " + (.id|tostring) + ")"' "$HERE/lib/last.json"

echo "== 1/8 Indstillinger (sprog/tid/title) =="
api POST "/wp/v2/settings" '{"title":"Warpstorm","description":"Unofficial Warhammer 40K fan site — beginner guides, army picks and starter sets","language":"da_DK","timezone":"Europe/Copenhagen"}' \
  && echo "  OK: title/language=da_DK/timezone=Europe/Copenhagen" || FAILS=$((FAILS+1))
sleep "$SLEEP"

echo "== 2/8 Plugins =="
PLUGINS="seo-by-rank-math wpforms-lite google-site-kit imagify"
[ "${JETPACK:-0}" = "1" ] && PLUGINS="$PLUGINS jetpack"
[ "${SHORTPIXEL:-0}" = "1" ] && PLUGINS="shortpixel-image-optimiser $PLUGINS imagify"
for slug in $PLUGINS; do
  if api GET "/wp/v2/plugins?search=$slug" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    inst="$(jq -r '[.[] | select(.plugin | startswith("'$slug'"))][0].plugin // empty' "$HERE/lib/last.json" 2>/dev/null)"
  else inst=""; fi
  if [ -n "$inst" ]; then
    st="$(jq -r --arg p "$inst" '.[] | select(.plugin==$p) | .status' "$HERE/lib/last.json" 2>/dev/null)"
    if [ "$st" = "active" ]; then echo "  OK: $slug allerede aktiv"; else
      api PUT "/wp/v2/plugins/$inst" '{"status":"active"}' && echo "  OK: $slug aktiveret" || FAILS=$((FAILS+1)); fi
  else
    api POST "/wp/v2/plugins" "{\"slug\":\"$slug\",\"status\":\"active\"}" \
      && echo "  OK: $slug installeret + aktiveret" || { echo "  ! $slug FEJLEDE (fortsætter)"; FAILS=$((FAILS+1)); }
  fi
  sleep "$SLEEP"
done

echo "== 3/8 Tema: Twenty Twenty-Five =="
if api GET "/wp/v2/themes?status=active" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  cur="$(jq -r '.[0].stylesheet // empty' "$HERE/lib/last.json" 2>/dev/null)"
  if [ "$cur" = "twentytwentyfive" ]; then echo "  OK: TT5 er allerede aktivt";
  else
    api POST "/wp/v2/themes" '{"stylesheet":"twentytwentyfive"}' && echo "  OK: TT5 aktiveret" \
      || { api PUT "/wp/v2/themes/twentytwentyfive" '{}' && echo "  OK: TT5 aktiveret (PUT)" || FAILS=$((FAILS+1)); }
  fi
fi
sleep "$SLEEP"

echo "== 4/8 Kategorier =="
cat_add() { # navn|slug
  local name="${1%%|*}" slug="${1#*|}" id
  id="$(get_id_by_slug categories "$slug")"
  if [ -n "$id" ]; then echo "  OK: $name (findes, id $id)"; else
    api POST "/wp/v2/categories" "{\"name\":\"$name\",\"slug\":\"$slug\"}" \
      && id="$(jq -r '.id' "$HERE/lib/last.json")" && echo "  OK: $name (id $id)" || FAILS=$((FAILS+1))
  fi
  [ -n "$id" ] && printf '%s=%s\n' "$name" "$id" >> "$MAP"
}
cat_add "Lore|lore"; sleep 1
cat_add "Hære|haere"; sleep 1
cat_add "Strategi|strategi"; sleep 1
cat_add "Hobby|hobby"; sleep 1
cat_add "Nyheder|nyheder"; sleep 1
cat_add "Guides|guides"; sleep 1

echo "== 5/8 Sider (status: $STATUS_DRAFT) =="
for f in "$HERE"/payloads/pages/*.json; do
  slug="$(jq -r '.slug' "$f")"; title="$(jq -r '.title' "$f")"
  id="$(get_id_by_slug pages "$slug")"
  if [ -n "$id" ]; then echo "  OK: side '$title' (findes, id $id)"; continue; fi
  api POST "/wp/v2/pages" "$(cat "$f" | jq -c '. + {status:"'$STATUS_DRAFT'"}')" \
    && echo "  OK: side '$title' (id $(jq -r '.id' "$HERE/lib/last.json"))" || FAILS=$((FAILS+1))
  sleep "$SLEEP"
done

echo "== 6/8 Grimdark CSS + permalinks (helper-plugin) =="
PLUGIN_ID=""
if api GET "/wp/v2/plugins?search=warpstorm-setup" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  PLUGIN_ID="$(jq -r '[.[] | select(.plugin | startswith("warpstorm-setup"))][0].plugin // empty' "$HERE/lib/last.json" 2>/dev/null)"
fi
if [ -n "$PLUGIN_ID" ]; then
  echo "  OK: helper-plugin findes ($PLUGIN_ID)"
else
  up="$(curl -sS -u "$AUTH" -X POST -F "package=@$HERE/plugin/warpstorm-setup.zip" \
       -o "$HERE/lib/last.json" -w "%{http_code}" "$BASE/wp-json/wp/v2/plugins" 2>&1 | tail -1)"
  if [ "$up" = "200" ] || [ "$up" = "201" ]; then
    PLUGIN_ID="$(jq -r '.plugin // empty' "$HERE/lib/last.json" 2>/dev/null)"
    echo "  OK: helper-plugin uploadet ($PLUGIN_ID)"
  else
    echo "  ! Multipart-upload fejlede (HTTP $up) — CSS tages via global-styles; permalinks sættes manuelt senere"
    FAILS=$((FAILS+1))
  fi
fi
if [ -n "$PLUGIN_ID" ]; then
  api PUT "/wp/v2/plugins/$PLUGIN_ID" '{"status":"active"}' && echo "  OK: helper-plugin aktiv" || FAILS=$((FAILS+1))
  sleep "$SLEEP"
  api POST "/warpstorm/v1/setup" '{"front":"forside","blog":"start-her"}' \
    && jq -r '"  OK: setup → " + (.permalink_structure // "?") + " · front=" + ((.page_on_front // "-")|tostring) + " · blog=" + ((.page_for_posts // "-")|tostring)' "$HERE/lib/last.json" \
    || FAILS=$((FAILS+1))
else
  echo "  - Fallback: CSS injectes via global-styles"
  CSSJSON="$(jq -Rs . < "$HERE/css/grimdark-v1.1.css")"
  api POST "/wp/v2/global-styles" "{\"version\":2,\"settings\":{},\"styles\":{\"css\":$CSSJSON}}" \
    && echo "  OK: Grimdark CSS v1.1 via global-styles" || FAILS=$((FAILS+1))
fi
sleep "$SLEEP"

echo "== 7/8 Artikler 1-5 (status: $STATUS_DRAFT) =="
for f in "$HERE"/payloads/articles/*.json; do
  slug="$(jq -r '.slug' "$f")"; title="$(jq -r '.title' "$f")"
  id="$(get_id_by_slug posts "$slug")"
  if [ -n "$id" ]; then echo "  OK: artikel '$title' (findes, id $id)"; continue; fi
  cats=""; first=1
  for name in $(jq -r '.categories[]' "$f"); do
    cid="$(grep -F "$name=" "$MAP" | head -1 | cut -d= -f2)"
    [ -n "$cid" ] && { [ $first = 1 ] && cats="$cid" || cats="$cats,$cid"; first=0; }
  done
  body="$(cat "$f" | jq -c '. + {status:"'$STATUS_DRAFT'"} + {categories:['"${cats:-0}"']}' )"
  api POST "/wp/v2/posts" "$body" \
    && echo "  OK: artikel '$title' → id $(jq -r '.id' "$HERE/lib/last.json") (cats: ${cats:-none})" || FAILS=$((FAILS+1))
  sleep "$SLEEP"
done

echo "== 8/8 Verifikation =="
api GET "/wp/v2/posts?status=$STATUS_DRAFT&per_page=20&orderby=modified" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  && echo "  Posts ($STATUS_DRAFT): $(jq -r 'map(.slug)|join(", ")' "$HERE/lib/last.json" 2>/dev/null)"
api GET "/wp/v2/pages?status=$STATUS_DRAFT&per_page=20" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  && echo "  Pages ($STATUS_DRAFT): $(jq -r 'map(.slug)|join(", ")' "$HERE/lib/last.json" 2>/dev/null)"
api GET "/wp/v2/settings" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  && echo "  Settings: lang=$(jq -r '.language' "$HERE/lib/last.json") tz=$(jq -r '.timezone' "$HERE/lib/last.json") front=$(jq -r '.show_on_front' "$HERE/lib/last.json")"
api GET "/wp/v2/themes?status=active" >/dev/null 2>&1 \
  && echo "  Tema: $(jq -r '.[0].stylesheet' "$HERE/lib/last.json")"

echo ""
[ $FAILS = 0 ] && echo "✅ GRIMDARK-PAKKEN KØRT — 0 fejl. Artikler ligger som drafts." \
              || echo "⚠️ FÆRDIG MED $FAILS FEJL — se ovenfor."

# Grimdark Pakke — warpstorm.online

Én-kommando deploy-pakke til Warpstorm (Warhammer 40K-fansitet). Alt er forberedt; intet rører sitet før app-passwordet er landet.

## Indhold
- `deploy.sh` — POSIX-sh-script der kører hele sekvensen (trin 0-8 i RUNBOOK.md), idempotent
- `RUNBOOK.md` — trin-for-trin med exact REST-kald + fallbacks (køres af Juno)
- `payloads/articles/` — 5 færdige artikler som WP-REST-payloads (draft, HTML, interlinks, excerpts)
- `payloads/pages/` — 6 side-payloads (forside, start-her, om, kontakt, privatlivspolitik, affiliate-disclosure)
- `css/grimdark-v1.1.css` — Grimdark CSS v1 + base/grim-komponenter (sort #0A0A0C, rød #8C1D2C, guld #B8963E)
- `plugin/warpstorm-setup/` + `.zip` — helper-plugin: permalinks /%postname%/, statisk forside, CSS-enqueue
- `tools/md2html.py` — markdown→HTML-konverter (kør via Juno scripts ved nye artikler)
- `tools/mkzip.py` — genbygger plugin-zippet

## Aktivering (når Henning har lavet app-password)
1. Gem `bruger:app-password` i `/workspace/warpstorm/.wp-auth-online`
2. Sig "kør Grimdark-pakken"

## IP-regler (binding)
Uofficiel fanside + disclosure på alt · ingen GW-logoer/billeder i shop · generiske produktnavne · rel="sponsored nofollow" på affiliate-links.

# Grimdark-pakken — RUNBOOK (køres af Juno)

**Trigger:** Så snart app-password til warpstorm.online er landet i `/workspace/warpstorm/.wp-auth-online` (format `bruger:xxxx app-password`).
**Kommando til Henning:** bare "kør Grimdark-pakken".

Regler: REST-kald med 3 s mellemrum · ved 429/503: vent 60 s og prøv igen · alt verificeres i svarene.

## Trin 0 — Preflight
1. `GET /wp-json` → site-navn/URL bekræftes
2. `GET /wp-json/wp/v2/users/me?context=edit` → auth virker + admin-rettigheder

## Trin 1 — Indstillinger
`POST /wp-json/wp/v2/settings` body: `{"title":"Warpstorm","description":"Unofficial Warhammer 40K fan site — beginner guides, army picks and starter sets","language":"da_DK","timezone":"Europe/Copenhagen"}`

## Trin 2 — Plugins (install+aktiv via REST, slug-baseret)
seo-by-rank-math · wpforms-lite · google-site-kit · imagify
(`JETPACK=1` tilføjer jetpack; `SHORTPIXEL=1` swapper imagify ud)
- check: `GET /wp/v2/plugins?search=<slug>` → aktiv? spring over
- ellers: `POST /wp/v2/plugins {"slug":"<slug>","status":"active"}`

## Trin 3 — Tema TT5
- `GET /wp/v2/themes?status=active` → hvis ikke twentytwentyfive:
- `POST /wp/v2/themes {"stylesheet":"twentytwentyfive"}` (fallback `PUT /wp/v2/themes/twentytwentyfive`)

## Trin 4 — Kategorier (Lore, Hære, Strategi, Hobby, Nyheder, Guides)
Pr. kategori: `GET /wp/v2/categories?slug=<slug>` → ellers `POST /wp/v2/categories {"name":"X","slug":"y"}`
Slugs: lore, haere, strategi, hobby, nyheder, guides. Gem id-map i `lib/catmap.env`.

## Trin 5 — Sider (som drafts)
Payloads klar i `payloads/pages/` (forside, start-her, om, kontakt, privatlivspolitik, affiliate-disclosure).
Pr. side: `GET /wp/v2/pages?slug=X` → ellers `POST /wp/v2/pages` med payload + `{"status":"draft"}`.

## Trin 6 — Grimdark CSS v1.1 + permalinks
Primær: upload `plugin/warpstorm-setup.zip` → `POST /wp/v2/plugins` (multipart `-F "package=@…"`) → aktivér → `POST /wp-json/warpstorm/v1/setup {"front":"forside","blog":"start-her"}` (sætter `/%postname%/`, statisk forside, flush rewrites, enqueue CSS).
Fallback (hvis multipart fejler): CSS via `POST /wp/v2/global-styles` `{"version":2,"settings":{},"styles":{"css":"<css>"}}`; permalinks sættes derefter i wp-admin (Settings → Permalinks → Save) — Juno klarer det via browser-session.
NB: global-styles-kaldet og plugin-uploaden kan give transient 401/500 → retry.

## Trin 7 — Artikler 1-5 (drafts)
Payloads i `payloads/articles/*.json` (HTML-konverteret, interlinks intakt, kategorier mappet via catmap).
Pr. artikel: `GET /wp/v2/posts?slug=X&status=draft,publish` → ellers `POST /wp/v2/posts` payload+status.
Billeder: IMAGE-01..12 peger på `/wp-content/uploads/IMAGE-…` — upload senere med samme filnavne, links knækker ikke.

## Trin 8 — Verifikation
- `GET /wp/v2/posts?status=draft` → 5 artikler
- `GET /wp/v2/pages?status=draft` → 6 sider
- `GET /wp/v2/settings` → language da_DK, timezone Europe/Copenhagen, show_on_front page
- `GET /wp/v2/themes?status=active` → twentytwentyfive
- `GET /wp/v2/plugins` → 4-5 aktive
- live check: `https://warpstorm.online/` HTML indeholder grimdark-baggrund (#0A0A0C) efter publish (kan først ses ved udgivelse pga. cache)

## Efter kørslen (ikke i denne pakke)
- Slet helper-plugin (valgfrit, efter verificering)
- Rank Math setup-wizard + Site Kit kræver OAuth (Henning-trin)
- Permalinks-fallback hvis plugin-upload fejlede
- Billedgenerering (IMAGE-01..12) og upload
- Publish = PUBLISH=1 eller udgiv drafts én for én

<?php
/**
 * Plugin Name: Warpstorm Setup (Juno Grimdark Package)
 * Description: One-shot helper: sets Post-name permalinks + static front page and enqueues Grimdark CSS v1.1. Safe to delete after use.
 * Version: 1.0.0
 * Author: Juno
 */

if ( ! defined( 'ABSPATH' ) ) { exit; }

add_action( 'rest_api_init', function () {
	register_rest_route( 'warpstorm/v1', '/setup', array(
		'methods'             => 'POST',
		'permission_callback' => function () { return current_user_can( 'manage_options' ); },
		'callback'            => 'wps_setup_run',
	) );
} );

function wps_setup_run( WP_REST_Request $req ) {
	$out = array();

	$target = '/%postname%/';
	if ( get_option( 'permalink_structure' ) !== $target ) {
		update_option( 'permalink_structure', $target );
		$out['permalink_structure'] = 'set';
	} else {
		$out['permalink_structure'] = 'already-set';
	}

	update_option( 'show_on_front', 'page' );
	$out['show_on_front'] = 'page';

	$front = get_page_by_path( sanitize_title( $req->get_param( 'front' ) ? $req->get_param( 'front' ) : 'forside' ) );
	if ( $front ) { update_option( 'page_on_front', $front->ID ); $out['page_on_front'] = (int) $front->ID; }

	$blog = get_page_by_path( sanitize_title( $req->get_param( 'blog' ) ? $req->get_param( 'blog' ) : 'start-her' ) );
	if ( $blog ) { update_option( 'page_for_posts', $blog->ID ); $out['page_for_posts'] = (int) $blog->ID; }

	flush_rewrite_rules( true );
	$out['rewrite_flushed'] = true;
	return rest_ensure_response( $out );
}

add_action( 'wp_enqueue_scripts', function () {
	wp_register_style( 'grimdark-v1', plugins_url( 'grimdark-v1.css', __FILE__ ), array(), '1.1' );
	wp_enqueue_style( 'grimdark-v1' );
} );

add_filter( 'body_class', function ( $classes ) {
	$classes[] = 'grim-skin';
	return $classes;
} );



import os, zipfile

SRC = "workspace/warpstorm/deploy/plugin/warpstorm-setup"
OUT = "workspace/warpstorm/deploy/plugin/warpstorm-setup.zip"

def main(input):
    if os.path.exists(OUT):
        os.remove(OUT)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(OUT, "w", zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as z:
        for fn in sorted(os.listdir(SRC)):
            z.write(os.path.join(SRC, fn), "warpstorm-setup/" + fn)
    with zipfile.ZipFile(OUT) as z:
        names = z.namelist()
        bad = z.testzip()
        php = z.read("warpstorm-setup/warpstorm-setup.php").decode("utf-8")[:60]
    return {"files": names, "testzip": bad, "php_head": php, "bytes": os.path.getsize(OUT)}

Short answer: If you want the easiest start in Warhammer 40,000, pick Space Marines — they're forgiving, well-documented, and every starter box is built around them. Want something cooler and just as easy? Necrons are the best second choice: simple rules, tough models, and a striking look that paints up fast. Both armies let you learn the game without punishing mistakes.

Disclosure: Grimdark Builds is an unofficial fan site. Some links on this page are affiliate links — if you buy through them, we may earn a small commission at no extra cost to you. We are not affiliated with or endorsed by Games Workshop.

Why Your First Army Matters More Than You Think

Your first army decides whether you stay in the hobby or quietly quit after three months. Beginners who pick an army that's cheap to collect, easy to paint, and forgiving to play finish their first 1,000 points and actually get games in. Beginners who pick a horde of 80 fiddly models or a fragile elite army that punishes every mistake often stall out.

So "best" here means three things:

  • Easy to build and paint — large, chunky models with simple colour schemes
  • Forgiving in-game — tough units that survive beginner mistakes
  • Cheap to start — a single starter box gets you playable

Beginner Army Comparison Table

Pick #1: Space Marines — The Safe, Smart Choice

Space Marines are the army Games Workshop builds everything around, and that's exactly why they're the best beginner pick:

  • Every starter set includes them. The introductory boxes (like the current Recruit/Ultimate starter sets) are Space Marines vs. Tyranids or Space Marines vs. Necrons — so the cheapest way into the game already hands you half an army.
  • They forgive mistakes. Marines are tough, hit reliably, and have decent armour saves. When you misplay — and you will — your army doesn't evaporate.
  • Endless free resources. More tutorials, army lists, painting guides and community advice exist for Space Marines than any other faction combined.
  • Simple colour schemes. A blue, green or red armour scheme with a wash and a highlight looks great with beginner-level skills.

Best for: players who want to learn the rules, meet people at their local store, and never worry about "did I pick wrong?"

How to start Space Marines

1. Buy a starter box (cheapest way to get models, dice, ruler and rules in one purchase). 2. Assemble 10–15 models, paint them with a simple 3-colour scheme — don't chase "golden demon" quality yet. 3. Play small games (500 points) to learn movement, shooting and charge rules. 4. Expand to 1,000 points with one box of Intercessors and one vehicle.

Pick #2: Necrons — The Cool Alternative

If "generic super soldiers" doesn't excite you, Necrons are the best beginner army in the game on pure value:

  • Simple rules, durable models. Reanimation protocols let you shrug off damage — very forgiving while you're learning.
  • Skeleton robots paint fast. A silver basecoat, green accents and a wash gets you a table-ready army in a weekend. Perfect for new painters.
  • Strong start boxes. The Necrons half of the main starter set alone gets you a legal combat patrol-sized force.
  • They look incredible on a shelf. Let's be honest — glowing green eyes and living-metal heroes are a huge motivation boost.

Best for: hobbyists who want an army that looks finished with minimal painting skill, and players who like resilient, no-nonsense armies.

How to start Necrons

1. Grab the Necrons half of a starter set (or a Necrons combat patrol box). 2. Paint a test model first: spray, leadbelcher-style basecoat, green glow accents, black wash. 3. Play 500-point games — Necron durability hides beginner errors. 4. Add a big centre-piece (a Monolith or C'tan) once you hit 1,000 points.

Which Should You Pick?

There is no wrong answer between these two. Both are top-tier beginner armies; pick the one whose models make you want to paint tonight.

FAQ — Best Warhammer 40K Army for Beginners

What is the easiest Warhammer 40K army for a complete beginner? Space Marines. They're tough in-game, easy to build and paint, and every starter product is designed around them. Necrons are a close second with simpler model counts and fast paint schemes.

Is Warhammer 40K expensive for beginners? You can start for roughly $100–150 with a starter box, clippers, glue and 3–4 paint pots. That covers your first playable 500-point games. Expanding to 1,000 points adds another $80–150 over a few months.

Should I pick my army based on looks or rules? Looks. Rules change with every balance dataslate; you'll be painting and staring at these models for years. Both Marines and Necrons pass the rules test anyway, so pick the aesthetic you love.

How long does it take to paint a first army? A simple 500-point army (about 15–20 models) takes a beginner 10–15 hours with a basic basecoat/wash/highlight scheme. Batch-painting one unit at a time makes this painless.

Can I play Space Marines and Necrons together? Not in the same list, but you can absolutely collect both — many hobbyists do. Starter boxes for both armies come with the same core rules, so nothing is wasted.

Are Necrons good for beginners in 2026? Yes — simple army rules, durable models, forgiving reanimation mechanics and one of the fastest paint schemes in the game make them one of the two best beginner picks.

Short answer: Start Warhammer 40K in four steps: buy a starter box (around $100–150), build and paint 10–15 models with a simple scheme, learn the core rules through 500-point games, then grow to a full 1,000-point army. Don't plan a 2,000-point list or buy a huge haul on day one — the hobby rewards small, finished steps.

Step 1: Buy a Starter Box (Not a Big Haul)

The single biggest beginner mistake is buying $400 of models before playing a single game. A starter box gives you everything in one purchase:

  • Two small armies (so you can play with a friend or demo both sides)
  • Dice, measuring ruler and the core rules
  • A clear path: assemble → paint → play

What to buy: the current main starter set (Space Marines vs. Tyranids or Space Marines vs. Necrons, depending on the edition box in stores). Add side cutters, plastic glue and 3–4 paint pots if the box doesn't include them — budget another $30–40.

👉 Not sure which faction? Read Best Warhammer 40K Army for Beginners — short version: Space Marines for the safest start, Necrons for the best-looking easy army.

Step 2: Build Your First 10–15 Models

Assembly tips that save beginners hours of pain:

  • Cut sprues with side cutters, never twist parts off — twisted plastic leaves marks and stress lines.
  • Dry-fit before gluing. Test that legs, torso and arms line up before any glue touches plastic.
  • One unit at a time. Ten finished models beat fifty half-assembled ones rotting in a drawer.
  • Keep the sprues. They hold small parts (pouches, grenades, bases) you'll want later.

Step 3: Paint Them "Table-Ready" (Not Perfect)

Beginner paint formula that always looks decent:

1. Spray undercoat (black or grey primer) 2. Basecoat one main colour (drybrush or two thin coats) 3. Wash (a shade paint like Nuln Oil — this does 50% of the work for you) 4. Highlight edges lightly with a lighter colour

Total time: 20–30 minutes per model. A full 500-point army takes a weekend or two of evenings. "Table-ready" — not competition-level — is the goal. Your models will look better than you expect from three feet away, which is exactly how anyone will see them across a table.

Step 4: Learn the Rules With Small Games

  • Start at 500 points. Small games teach movement, shooting, charges and objectives without overwhelming you.
  • Use the free core rules. Games Workshop publishes the basic rules as free PDFs — you don't need the full rulebook on day one.
  • Play your local store. Most stores run beginner nights or will happily teach a new player. Turn up with painted models and you'll always find an opponent.
  • Lose your first five games. It's the standard experience. You're learning objectives and sequencing, not winning yet.

Step 5: Grow to 1,000 Points (Over Months, Not Days)

Once you've played a handful of small games:

  • Expand the units you actually enjoyed playing
  • Add one big centrepiece model (a tank, a Monolith, a big hero) — it's the fun reward of the hobby
  • Aim for 1,000 points as your first "real" army — it's the most common casual game size

Budget reality: a complete 1,000-point army typically lands around $250–400 all-in (models, paint, tools), spread over 2–4 months. That's much cheaper than most hobbies — and cheaper than buying everything at once and quitting.

Common Beginner Mistakes to Avoid

  • Buying a meta list off the internet before knowing how you like to play
  • Skipping paint to "get gaming faster" — grey plastic armies kill motivation
  • Playing only big games — you learn faster in ten 500-point games than two 2,000-point ones
  • Perfectionism on the first models — your first squad is allowed to be ugly. Finish it.

FAQ — How to Start Warhammer 40K

How much does it cost to start Warhammer 40K? Around $130–190 to start properly: a starter box ($100–150) plus basic tools and paints ($30–40). Your first 500-point army is playable with nothing else.

Is Warhammer 40K hard to learn? The core loop (move, shoot, charge, fight, score objectives) is learnable in one evening. Mastery takes months, but the free core rules plus a couple of small games are enough to play properly.

Do I need the full rulebook to start? No. The core rules are free from Games Workshop, and starter boxes include a trimmed-down rules set. Buy the full rulebook when you're hooked, not before.

How long until I can play a real game? One to three weekends: assemble one box (an evening or two), paint a simple scheme (a weekend), then book a 500-point game. Playing unpainted models is also fully accepted at stores.

Should I start with 10th edition? Yes — this is the simplest edition for beginners in years, with free core rules, clean datacards and an active beginner scene. There's no reason to wait.

Can I play alone? Casual solo practice games work fine for learning rules, and kill-team-sized skirmish modes are popular solo. But the social side — store nights, tournaments, painting days — is half the hobby, so find a local opponent early.

Why Space Marines Are the Beginner Army

Every edition, every starter box and half of all hobby content on the internet is built around Space Marines. For a beginner, that translates into three real advantages:

1. Tough on the table. Good armour saves and decent toughness mean your mistakes don't delete your army in one enemy phase. 2. Cheap and available. Starter sets, Combat Patrol boxes and second-hand markets are flooded with Marines — the easiest army to buy and sell. 3. Infinite learning material. Whatever question you have — painting, list-building, tactics — someone has answered it with photos and videos.

Your First 1,000 Points (Simple Starter List)

A forgiving, no-tricks 1,000-point core that plays well while you learn:

Exact point values shift with each balance dataslate — check the current free points PDF before a game. The structure (battleline core + one heavy + one fast unit) stays correct between updates.

Expansion path: at 2,000 points add a vehicle block (Redemptor-style Dreadnought or Repulsor) and a second Battleline squad. Buy one box at a time and paint it before the next.

Paint Scheme: Simple and Sharp

The classic mistake is choosing a scheme with ten steps. Pick a one-colour armour scheme:

  • Basecoat the whole model in your chapter colour (two thin coats)
  • Wash with a black or brown shade — instant depth
  • Drybrush or edge-highlight with a lighter tone
  • Details last: gun metal, eye lenses (a dot of colour), gold on the shoulder trim

Two evenings of painting gets ten models done. Save the freehand banners and glow effects for squad number three, not squad number one.

Playing Your First Games

  • Keep the army in a castle formation early: Marines are durable enough to hold ground and shoot — the simplest way to learn objectives.
  • Charge only when you're sure you'll win. Learning melee math the hard way is expensive.
  • Score objectives, not kills. Beginners lose games by chasing kills; the mission rewards standing on circles.

Common Marine Beginner Mistakes

  • Spreading units across the whole board — Marines win by concentrating fire and holding midfield
  • Leaving the Captain home — leader buffs make your Battleline units dramatically better
  • Painting checkered chapter schemes too early — chunky colour blocks first, detail later

FAQ — Space Marines for Beginners

Are Space Marines good for beginners? Yes — the best choice. They're forgiving in-game, easy to build and paint, and every starter product includes them. You'll never struggle to find advice, opponents or spare models.

How much does a 1,000-point Space Marine army cost? Roughly $250–400 including tools and paints, less if you start from a starter box or buy second-hand. The starter boxes alone cover the first 500 points.

Which Space Marine chapter should I paint? One with a simple scheme: a solid blue (Ultramarines-style), green or red. Save complex chapter schemes for later armies. Homebrew chapters are fully legitimate — invent your own colours.

Are Space Marines still strong in the current edition? Marines are always a mid-to-strong, well-supported faction — Games Workshop balances around them first. As a beginner, their forgiving durability matters far more than meta tier lists.

What do I buy after the starter box? One box of Intercessors and one heavy/vehicle box gets you to a real 1,000 points. Buy, build, paint, repeat — one box at a time.

Space Marines vs. Necrons for a first army? Both are top beginner picks. Marines win on community support and starter-box availability; Necrons win on looks and fastest paint scheme. Read our head-to-head comparison.

Why Necrons Are a Perfect First Army

Necrons are ancient, undying robot legions — and mechanically, they're built for people learning the game:

1. Reanimation Protocols forgive mistakes. Your fallen warriors stand back up. While you're learning positioning, your army heals your errors. 2. One simple army rule, clean datacards. Fewer nested special rules than almost any other faction — you spend game nights learning 40K, not Necron exceptions. 3. Fastest paint scheme in the game. Silver basecoat + black wash + green accents = table-ready. No faction gets from sprue to tabletop faster. 4. Small model count. Most Necron lists run fewer models than horde armies — less assembly, less painting, less cost per finished game.

Your First 1,000 Points (Simple Starter List)

Point values change with each dataslate — always check the current free points file. The structure (Warrior core + leader + one melee + one fast + one heavy) is durable across updates.

Expansion path: add a Monolith or a C'tan Shard as your 2,000-point centrepiece. One big model per purchase — paint it before the next.

Paint Scheme: The Weekend Army

The famous "one weekend" Necron recipe:

1. Spray black or grey primer 2. Basecoat everything silver (one coat is fine on metal) 3. Wash with black shade — the wash does the entire "depth" job 4. Glow accents: drybrush the weapon coils and eyes in green, add a second lighter pass on the brightest spots

Fifteen models in two evenings, and they look like a proper undying legion. Black-and-green variants, brass trims and rusty "tomb world" versions all come later — the base scheme is genuinely this easy.

Playing Your First Games

  • Warriors in the middle. They're your objectives team — march them up the board and let reanimation punish your opponent's shooting.
  • Shoot the dangerous stuff, ignore the chaff. Necron guns are good; the beginner mistake is wasting them on cheap enemy units.
  • Don't fear melee. Even when Destroyers die, that's their job — buying time for your Warriors to score.

Common Necron Beginner Mistakes

  • Spending huge points on one giant unit too early — learn with a balanced core first
  • Forgetting reanimation rolls — it's the faction's whole identity; write it on your army roster
  • Leaving the Overlord's buff out of range — keep leaders glued to the Warriors

FAQ — Necrons for Beginners

Are Necrons good for beginners? Yes — arguably the best non-Marine start. Simple rules, durable units and a fast paint scheme make them ideal while you're learning movement, shooting and objectives.

How much does a 1,000-point Necron army cost? Around $250–350 including paints and tools. The Necrons half of a starter box plus one or two boxes gets you most of the way there.

What's the easiest Necron paint scheme? Silver basecoat, black wash, glowing green accents. It's the most famous beginner scheme in the hobby for a reason — fifteen models in a weekend, looking genuinely good.

Necrons vs. Space Marines for a first army? Both excellent. Marines: maximum community support and starter availability. Necrons: better looks-per-hour-of-painting and fewer models to manage. Read our full comparison.

Do Necrons have complicated rules? Their core rules are simple — reanimation is one mechanic, and most units are straightforward shooting or melee. You'll spend more time learning 40K's universal rules than Necron-specific exceptions.

What do I buy after the starter box? One Warrior box and one fast or melee box gets you to 1,000 points. Add your first big centrepiece (Monolith or C'tan) as the reward for finishing your paint queue.
